text: What is GSE309890 about, and what files can I actually download?
I'll look up GSE309890 in GEO to get its metadata and downloadable files.

## Abstract

This report resolves the GEO Series accession GSE309890 to its registered metadata and its downloadable files. Using a single GEO summary query routed through the NCBI E-utilities `gds` database, I retrieved the study title, summary, organism, platform, sample list, and the contents of its FTP supplementary directory. GSE309890 is an expression-profiling-by-high-throughput-sequencing study in *Escherichia coli* str. K-12 substr. MG1655, examining how the SSRI antidepressant sertraline biases antibiotic resistance emergence through rewiring of the pentose phosphate pathway, with transketolase A (tktA) identified as a target for restoring susceptibility. The Series comprises 6 samples: 3 controls and 3 adaptive-evolution replicates sampled at day 40. The record is linked to BioProject PRJNA1363958 and carries no linked PubMed record. GEO's API returns metadata only; processed expression values exist solely in the FTP supplementary tree. One supplementary file is registered: `GSE309890_FPKMs_allSamples.csv.gz` (510K), holding FPKM values for all samples. The study is scheduled to become public on 2026/02/01. The result matters because it identifies exactly which one file contains reusable expression data and confirms the biological scope before any download.

## I. Introduction

**Background.** GSE309890 is a Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) Series—the unit GEO uses to group the samples of one study. It profiles *Escherichia coli* str. K-12 substr. MG1655 by high-throughput sequencing to investigate a metabolic mechanism linking the antidepressant sertraline to antibiotic resistance emergence. The question—what the study is about and what can actually be downloaded—matters because GEO's API returns descriptive metadata but not the expression values themselves, so identifying the correct file is a prerequisite for reuse.

**Literature Review.** No literature was retrieved for this query. The GEO record has no linked PubMed entry (`pubmed_ids: []`); the tool notes this typically indicates an unpublished or not-yet-indexed study and never means the study has no data.

**Knowledge Gap.** Before this query, the study's scope, sample structure, organism, and the existence and identity of downloadable processed-data files were unknown from the accession alone.

**Objective & Hypothesis.** Objective: resolve GSE309890 to its metadata and enumerate the files a user can download. No statistical hypothesis applies to a metadata-retrieval task.

## II. Materials and Methods

**Study Design.** A single database was appropriate: the accession is a GEO Series identifier, so I routed directly to GEO rather than searching. The GEO tool also lists the FTP supplementary directory, which is the only source of the processed values.

**Materials.** NCBI GEO, reached via the `geo_series` tool (backed by the E-utilities `esummary` call against the `gds` database, plus an FTP directory listing).

**Procedures.** One tool call: `geo_series` with `accession = "GSE309890"` and the default `list_files = true`.

**Statistical Analysis.** No statistics were computed. Counts reported (6 samples; 1 supplementary file) are read directly from the `sample_count`, `samples`, and `supplementary_files` fields of the returned record.

## III. Results

**Data Presentation.**

**Table 1. Study metadata for GSE309890.**

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Title | Antidepressant sertraline biases resistance emergence via stress-driven rewiring of the pentose phosphate pathway: tktA enables metabolic rollback |
| Organism | *Escherichia coli* str. K-12 substr. MG1655 |
| Experiment type | Expression profiling by high throughput sequencing |
| Platform | GPL24659 |
| Samples | 6 |
| BioProject | PRJNA1363958 |
| Linked PubMed | None |
| Public date | 2026/02/01 |

**Table 2. Samples in GSE309890.**

| Accession | Title |
|---|---|
| GSM9284457 | E. coli, control, rep1 |
| GSM9284458 | E. coli, control, rep2 |
| GSM9284459 | E. coli, control, rep3 |
| GSM9284460 | E. coli, adaptive evolution, 40day, rep1 |
| GSM9284461 | E. coli, adaptive evolution, 40day, rep2 |
| GSM9284462 | E. coli, adaptive evolution, 40day, rep3 |

**Table 3. Downloadable supplementary files.**

| File | Size | Last modified | URL |
|---|---|---|---|
| GSE309890_FPKMs_allSamples.csv.gz | 510K | 2025-11-14 11:10 | https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE309nnn/GSE309890/suppl/GSE309890_FPKMs_allSamples.csv.gz |

**Findings.** GSE309890 is an *E. coli* K-12 MG1655 RNA sequencing study on sertraline-driven antibiotic resistance and the pentose phosphate pathway. It contains 6 samples in two groups of 3 (control and day-40 adaptive evolution). One supplementary file is registered for download: a gzipped CSV of FPKM values for all samples (510K). The whole-directory FTP location is https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE309nnn/GSE309890/. The record links to BioProject PRJNA1363958 and has no linked PubMed entry.

## IV. Discussion

**Interpretation.** The objective is met: the study's subject and its downloadable content are both resolved. The single FPKM CSV is the only place the processed expression values exist, so it is the file to download for reuse.

**Context.** The record's sample titles (3 control, 3 day-40 adaptive-evolution replicates) are consistent with the summary's design comparing sertraline-primed evolved *E. coli* against controls.

**Limitations.** GEO's API returns metadata only; the FPKM values themselves were not inspected here, only the file listing. Raw sequencing reads are not among the GEO supplementary files—they would sit under BioProject PRJNA1363958 / SRA, not queried in this run. The study is embargoed until 2026/02/01, so FTP access may be restricted before that date. No PubMed record is linked, so no peer-reviewed description was retrievable.

**Conclusion & Future Directions.** GSE309890 is a 6-sample *E. coli* RNA-seq study of sertraline-induced resistance via the pentose phosphate pathway; the one downloadable processed-data file is `GSE309890_FPKMs_allSamples.csv.gz`. The next query worth running is a lookup of BioProject PRJNA1363958 in SRA to locate the raw sequencing runs and their FASTQ download links.

## References

[1] NCBI GEO, Series GSE309890 (esummary, db=gds, id=200309890): https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE309890
[2] NCBI GEO FTP supplementary directory for GSE309890: https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE309nnn/GSE309890/suppl/

## Acknowledgments

Data provided by the NCBI Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) and the depositing study authors, accessed via NCBI E-utilities and the GEO FTP service.
